//: fli check's ratchet — one number per rule, and a number may only ever fall.
//detail-read-dead: All six are `portal.get()` — web/src/routes/portal/[id], web/src/components/widgets/ServiceHealthBody, and the four screens that each report one adapter (git-activity, observability, dns, cloud-spend). It is not a row: it builds an entry from an adapter ping, over no model, so there is no node to watch and no announcement will ever arrive. The other nine on this app are record views, composed where the service answers more than the row (FJS-533).
//polymorphic-subject: AuditEvent.subjectType is the SERVICE name (api/src/core/hooks.ts), so the set grows with every service and an enum would refuse the first row a new service writes. The other four pairs in this schema are enums; this one is the exemption the rule names.
//package-model-drift: Both are `model Notification` against @frontierjs/notifications, both are the same deviation, and the package's own file anticipates it: EVERY id in this app is a uuid, so `id` and `contextId` are String where the package writes Int. The third difference the rule does not flag is the one worth knowing about anyway — `contextType` is a NotificationContext enum here rather than a free String, which is the package telling an app to constrain the half of a polymorphic pair that can be constrained. A column the package's own code starts writing would still be reported: this number is two, and a third finding fails.
//service-as-system: All four are `app.db.asSystem()` inside `api/**/services/**`, and all four are deliberate: api-keys/scopes.ts, hub/hub.service.ts, jobs/job-schedule.ts, metrics/metrics.service.ts. metrics.service.ts is not the hazard at all - MetricSeries, MetricPoint and MetricHour are junction's, carry no workspaceId column and are gated at 8, so there is no tenant to cross. The rule skips a whole app under `strategy database` for exactly that argument and cannot make it per MODEL, because the accessor comes off a lambda and chasing it would be a dataflow guess. hub.service.ts IS the cross-workspace tier, behind one requireSystemAdmin(). job-schedule.ts's is restoreSchedules, called once from app.ts at boot with no request in scope, and it must span every workspace or a tenant's scheduled jobs stop firing (FJS-327). scopes.ts's is apiKeyGuard, which reads the ApiKey row that DECIDES the caller's access - so it cannot be read through a client that access already scoped - and confines it by hand on the next line: a request naming a workspace other than the key's is Forbidden. This is a COUNT, so a legitimate site removed and an illegitimate one added nets to four; the four paths are named here so a diff that moves one shows.
//capability-ladder: Both are the exemption FJS-D146 names when it mandates this very check: a deliberately high floor under a grid. Server and Environment carry @@capabilities and @@gate("2.4.4.5"), and the failure the rule warns about needs a role that HOLDS a grant and sits BELOW the write level. Basecamp has none, and it is measured rather than argued: api/src/core/gate.ts maps viewer and billing to 2 and developer to 4, and api/src/core/capabilities.ts grants viewer [] and billing [] on both models - every grant is held at 4 or above, which is where the gate writes. So no grant is unreachable; the grid narrows WITHIN developers and admins, which is what the ladder cannot say. Flattening to @@gate("2") would make the hand-stamped grant table the only thing between a viewer and Server.delete, and seven writers stamp it. This is undecidable for fli check rather than merely unstated: the two maps are app source with no declared shape, so a rule reading them would be guessing at two module layouts. The number is 2, so a THIRD @@capabilities model fails - and the two role sets are named here so a role gaining a grant below level 4 makes this entry visibly false in the diff.
